questions.question:
Which of the following statements about the Mauryan Empire is true?

 
• Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire with Kautilya’s assistance.
 
• Bindusara expanded the empire to the southern part of India.
 
• Ashoka was known for his military conquests and promotion of Buddhism.
 
• The Nanda Dynasty was peacefully succeeded by the Mauryas.
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - 1, 2, and 3 only**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta Maurya established the Mauryan Empire with Kautilya’s assistance.**

 
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, with the strategic guidance of his advisor Kautilya (also known as Chanakya), overthrew the Nanda Dynasty and established the Mauryan Empire around 322 BCE.
 
• Kautilya's treatise, the "Arthashastra," is a significant source of knowledge on ancient Indian politics and governance.
 
 
 
• **Bindusara expanded the empire to the southern part of India.**
 
 
• Bindusara, the son of Chandragupta, extended the Mauryan Empire further south, covering a large part of the Indian subcontinent.
 
• His conquests included the Deccan region, although the extreme southern parts of India, such as Tamil Nadu and Kerala, remained outside his control.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka was known for his military conquests and promotion of Buddhism.**
 
 
• Ashoka, the grandson of Chandragupta, initially engaged in numerous military campaigns, the most notable being the Kalinga War.
 
• The devastation of the Kalinga War led Ashoka to embrace Buddhism and promote non-violence, compassion, and Dharma (moral law) throughout his empire.
 
• Ashoka's edicts, spread across the Indian subcontinent, reflect his dedication to Buddhist principles and governance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Nanda Dynasty was not peacefully succeeded by the Mauryas.**

 
 
• The transition from the Nanda Dynasty to the Mauryan Empire was marked by conflict and upheaval.
 
• Chandragupta Maurya, with Kautilya's support, led a revolt against the Nanda rulers, leading to their eventual overthrow and the establishment of the Mauryan Empire.

questions.question: Ashoka sent his son Mahendra and daughter Sanghmitra to spread the message of Dhamma to which of the following countries?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sri Lanka.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• **Mahendra** is credited with introducing **Theravada Buddhism** to Sri Lanka, which became the island’s dominant form of Buddhism.
 
• **Sanghamitra** also brought a sapling of the **sacred Bodhi tree **(under which Buddha attained enlightenment), which was planted in **Anuradhapura**, a sacred city in Sri Lanka. 
 
• **Mahendra’s mission** to Sri Lanka led to the conversion of **King Devanampiya Tissa,** the ruler of Sri Lanka, to **Buddhism.**
 
• The last **Mauryan** ruler who was a Buddhist was** Brihadratha.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta Maurya** founded the **Mauryan Empire** in **322 BCE**, overthrowing the **Nanda Dynasty.**
 
• **Chandragupta’s reign** was guided by his advisor **Chanakya (Kautilya)**, who authored the famous **Arthashastra**, a treatise on statecraft and governance.
 
• **Emperor Ashoka**, the most famous Mauryan ruler, embraced **Buddhism** after the Kalinga War and spread the message of Dhamma (Buddhist moral teachings) across Asia.
 
• The **Mauryan Empire** had a highly **centralized administration** with a well-structured bureaucracy and efficient taxation system.
 
• **Ashoka **issued** rock **and **pillar edicts** to communicate his policies and the **principles of Dhamma** across his empire in **Prakrit **and **Brahmi script**.
 
• The **Mauryan Empire** declined after the death of** Ashoka** and ended with **Brihadratha**, who was assassinated by his general **Pushyamitra Shunga** in **185 BCE**, marking the rise of the **Shunga Dynasty.**

questions.question:
Arrange the following texts chronologically:

A. Milindapanha

B. Manu Smriti

C. Yajnavalkya Smriti

D. Suryasiddhanta
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - B,A.C,D**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

 
• **Milindapanha**

 
 
• Milindapanha, also known as "The Questions of King Milinda,"
 
• is a Buddhist text dating back to around the 1st century BCE to the 1st century CE.
 
• It is a dialogue between King Milinda (Menander I) and the monk Nagasena.
 
 
 
• **Manu Smriti**
 
 
• The Manu Smriti, also known as the Laws of Manu,
 
• is an ancient Hindu text that dates back to around 200 BCE to 200 CE.
 
• It is one of the earliest and most authoritative texts on Hindu law and dharma.
 
 
 
• **Yajnavalkya Smriti**
 
 
• Yajnavalkya Smriti is another ancient Hindu legal text,
 
• believed to be composed around the 3rd to 5th centuries CE.
 
• It is known for its detailed treatment of civil, criminal, and procedural law.

questions.question: Pulakeshin II assumed the title of 'Dakshinapatheshvara' (lord of the south) after defeating which of the following rulers of north India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harshavardhana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• Pulakeshin II was a renowned ruler of the Chalukya dynasty in South India.

• He defeated Harshavardhana, the ruler of North India, on the banks of the Narmada river.

• After this victory, Pulakeshin II assumed the title of 'Dakshinapatheshvara' which means 'lord of the south'.

• Harshavardhana was a powerful ruler of the Vardhana dynasty who ruled over North India from 606 to 647 AD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Pulakeshin II**

• Pulakeshin II (reigned 610–642 AD) is considered one of the greatest kings of the Chalukya dynasty of Vatapi (modern Badami in Karnataka).

• He is known for his military conquests and efficient administration.

• His reign marked the high point of the Chalukya power in South India.

• Pulakeshin II's exploits are detailed in the Aihole inscription composed by his court poet Ravikirti.

• **Harshavardhana**

• Harshavardhana, also known as Harsha, ruled North India from 606 to 647 AD.

• He was a patron of art and culture and his court was adorned with scholars such as Banabhatta and Xuanzang.

• Harsha attempted to expand his kingdom into the Deccan but was thwarted by Pulakeshin II.

• His reign is considered a significant period in Indian history due to the cultural and economic developments that took place.

• **Title 'Dakshinapatheshvara'**

• The title 'Dakshinapatheshvara' means 'Lord of the South'.

• It signified Pulakeshin II's supremacy over the Deccan region after his victory over Harshavardhana.

• This title was significant as it marked the assertion of Chalukya power in the southern part of India.

• **Chalukya Dynasty**

• The Chalukya dynasty ruled large parts of southern and central India between the 6th and 12th centuries.

• They are known for their contribution to Indian architecture, particularly the rock-cut temples of Badami and the structural temples of Aihole and Pattadakal.

• The Chalukyas played a crucial role in the history of South India and maintained significant cultural and political influence during their reign.

• Founded during the Gupta period, it became one of the first residential universities in the world and attracted students from various regions.

• Samudragupta's southern campaign was a major military achievement, bringing large parts of southern India under Gupta control.

questions.question:
Match the Dynasties with Key Religious Sites:

 
 

 Column A
 Column B
 
 

 A. Ikshvakus
 Guntupalli Buddhist Vihara
 
 

 B. Salankayanas

 
 Vijayawada Cave Temples
 
 

 C. Brahatphalayanas

 
 Nagarjunakonda Stupas
 
 

 D. Vishnukundis

 
 Peddavegi Monastery
questions.solution:
**The correct answer is - A-3, B-1, C-4, D-2**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ikshvakus and Nagarjunakonda Stupas**

 
 
• The Ikshvakus were an ancient Indian dynasty that ruled the region of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Nagarjunakonda is an important Buddhist site with many stupas, monasteries, and other structures from the Ikshvaku period.
 
 
 
• **Salankayanas and Guntupalli Buddhist Vihara**
 
 
• The Salankayanas were a dynasty that ruled parts of Andhra Pradesh in ancient India.
 
• The Guntupalli Buddhist Vihara is a significant Buddhist monastic complex associated with the Salankayanas.
 
 
 
• **Brahatphalayanas and Peddavegi Monastery**
 
 
• The Brahatphalayanas were a minor dynasty in ancient Andhra Pradesh.
 
• Peddavegi Monastery is a Buddhist site linked with the Brahatphalayanas.
 
 
 
• **Vishnukundis and Vijayawada Cave Temples**
 
 
• The Vishnukundis were a dynasty that ruled over parts of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.
 
• The Vijayawada Cave Temples are notable rock-cut temples associated with the Vishnukundis.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ikshvakus**

 
 
• The Ikshvakus were successors to the Satavahanas in the Krishna-Guntur region.
 
• Nagarjunakonda is one of the main archaeological sites that provides insights into their reign.
 
 
 
• **Salankayanas**
 
 
• They ruled from around the 3rd to 5th centuries CE in the coastal Andhra region.
 
• Their association with Buddhist sites like Guntupalli underscores their patronage of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Brahatphalayanas**
 
 
• A relatively less known dynasty, they ruled during the 3rd and 4th centuries CE.
 
• Peddavegi Monastery is an important Buddhist site linked to them.
 
 
 
• **Vishnukundis**
 
 
• They were known for their contributions to art, culture, and architecture in Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The Vijayawada Cave Temples reflect their architectural style and religious patronage.

questions.question:
Which of the following aspect of Political Philosophy is covered in the book 'Arthashastra'?

1. Statecraft

2. Economic Policy

3. Military Strategy
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1, 2, and 3**____.__

__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The Arthashastra

 
 
• The Arthashastra is one of the earliest works of political realism to have been written, along with Sun Tzu's The Art of War and Machiavelli's The Prince.
 
• Kautilya Arthashastra is a unique treatise on the art of statecraft or governance, wherein every single aspect of human life is subject to the jurisdiction of the state.
 
• His detailed work clearly laid down an organizational set-up, and there was a clear-cut division of ethics and politics. 
 
• The 'Arthashastra' is a treasure of Political Philosophy. 
 
• It is considered the most comprehensive treatise on statecraft of classical times.
 
• The first-ever book written on Practice of Management, this treatise is also about foreign policy, administration, economic reforms, policies, and war.
 
• It is a primeval Indian discourse on statecraft, economic policy, and military strategy. 
 
• It was written in Sanskrit. 
 
• Kautilya's Arthasashtra was composed between the 3rd to 2nd Century B.C.
 
• It is mainly a work of the art of government.
 
• In his view, for the smooth functioning of administration and the welfare of the people, the king had to be acquainted with the four Vedas and four sciences of government (Anvikashaki, Trai, Varta, and Dandniti).

questions.question:
With reference to the Fa-Hien, consider the following statements:

1. He described his journey in his travelogue, A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms.

2. According to him, during the reigns of Samudragupta and Vikramaditya, the city of Pataliputra was an important centre.

Which of the above statement is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1 only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Fa-Hien **

 
• **He was a Chinese Buddhist monk and translator who travelled by foot from China to India**, visiting sacred Buddhist sites in Central Asia, the Indian subcontinent and Southeast Asia between** 399-412 CE** to acquire Buddhist texts.
 
• **He described his journey in his travelogue, A Record of Buddhist Kingdoms. *Hence, Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• He is also renowned for his pilgrimage to** Lumbini,** the birthplace of Gautama Buddha (modern Nepal). However, he **mentioned nothing about the Guptas.**
 
• His **visit **to India occurred **during the reign of Chandragupta II.**
 
• He chronicled his travels in a book filled with early Buddhist accounts as well as the geography and history of a number of countries along the Silk Road as they were at the turn of the fifth century CE.
 
• **In Middle India, he wrote about Taxila, Pataliputra, Mathura, and Kannauj.**
 
• He had described **Patliputra **in great detail.
 
• According to him, **during the reigns of Samudragupta, the city of Pataliputra was neglected, but during the reign of Chandragupta II, it was given top priority. ***Hence, Statement 2 is not correct.*
 
• He also mentioned the monks who were studying for their religious exams.
 
• Because the **towns of Magadha were the largest** in the Gangetic Plains, he wrote **Magadha as Central India.**

questions.question:
Which of the following pairs are correctly matched?

 
 

 
 **(Inscription/Event)**
 **(Time Period)**
 
 

 1.
 Prayag Prashasti by Harishena
 4th century CE
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**option 4.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**__**Literary Sources: **__

__Prayag Prashasti:__ 

__
 
• The** Prayag Prashasti** (also known as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription) by Harishena, is an inscription that was written in** 345 CE**.
 
• It is an eulogy to Samudragupta, one of the most prominent rulers of the Gupta Empire. ***Hence pair 1 is correctly matched.***

**Fa Xian: **__

__
 
• The Chinese traveller Fa Xian (also known as Faxian)'s account is from the** 5th century CE, not the 6th century**.
 
• Fa Xian visited India during the reign of Chandragupta II, journeying across many parts of India, and his writings provide crucial information about India's early history. *Hence pair 2 is incorrectly matched.*

**Mudrarakshasa:**__ 

__
 
• The Mudrarakshasa is a political drama written by Vishakhadatta likely in the late **4th to early 5th century CE.**
 
• It provides an account of Chandragupta Maurya's ascent to power, aided by his counsellor, Chanakya. *Hence pair 3 is correctly matched.*

**Harshacharita:**__ 

__
 
• Harshacharita was written by Banabhatta in the **7th century CE, not the 6th century CE**.
 
• It is a biographical account of the Indian emperor Harsha's life and is a significant source of historical information about that time. *Hence pair 4 is incorrectly matched.*

**Aihole Prashasti:**__ 

__
 
• The Aihole Prashasti of Ravikirti is from the 7th century CE.
 
• This inscription was created by the court poet and minister, Ravikirti under the rule of Chalukya King, Pulakeshin II. *Hence pair 5 is correctly matched.*

**Kavirajamarga:**__

 
• It is the earliest available work on rhetoric, poetics, and grammar in the Kannada language.
 
• It was authored by the Rashtrakuta King Amoghavarsha and the scholar Sri Vijaya in the **9th century CE**. *Hence pair 6 is incorrectly matched.*

*Therefore the correct answer is option 4*

questions.question:
With reference to the Silappadikaram, consider the following statements:

1. It was composed by a poet named Chithalai Chathanar, around 1800 years ago.

2. It is the story of a merchant named Kovalan, who lived in Puhar and fell in love with a courtesan named Madhavi.

3. It is one of the five great epics and the earliest poem in Tamil literature.

Which of the above statement is/are correct?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2 and 3 only**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Silappadikaram**

 
• It is a famous Tamil epic.
 
• **It was composed by a poet named Ilango,** around 1800 years ago**. *Hence, Statement 1 is not correct.***
 
• **It is the story of a merchant named Kovalan, who lived in Puhar and fell in love with a courtesan named Madhavi, neglecting his wife Kannagi. ***Hence, Statement 2 is correct.*
 
• Later, he and Kannagi left Puhar and went to Madurai, where he was wrongly accused of theft by the court jeweller of the Pandya king.
 
• The king** sentenced Kovalan **to death.
 
• Kannagi, who still loved him, was full of grief and anger at this injustice and **destroyed the entire city of Madurai.**
 
• It is **one of the five great epics and the earliest poem in Tamil literature. ***Hence, Statement 3 is correct.*
 
• The fifth-century Tamil epic** Silappadikaram praises the river Cauvery. **
 
• It features unusual **praise of the Sun, the Moon, the river Cauvery and the city of Poompuhar** at its beginning, the contemporary tradition being to praise a deity.
